old: A 1943 Australian threepence, struck in the middle of World War II. King George VI is on the front, and the back shows three stalks of wheat by George Kruger Gray, a design used since 1938 — before the war began. It's made of real silver, which is why it feels different from today's coins in your hand.

old: A 1969 French half franc. The front shows the Sower — a woman scattering seeds at sunrise, one of France's most loved coin designs, first drawn by Oscar Roty around 1887. The back carries France's motto: liberty, equality, brotherhood.

old: A 1993 German 1 Deutsche Mark. The eagle with outstretched wings is Germany's federal eagle, a symbol of strength; the oak sprigs are on the other side, framing the value. The Deutsche Mark was one of the world's most trusted currencies until the euro replaced it in 2002.

old: A 1989 French 10 franc piece. The front shows the Spirit of Liberty, taken from the gilded statue on top of the July Column at the Place de la Bastille in Paris. The back has the value 10F with liberty, equality, fraternity. It was one of France's first two-metal coins — a silvery center set in a golden ring.

old: A 1975 Jamaican 50 cent piece. The coat of arms shows a crocodile on a log on top, held up by a man and woman of the Taino people who lived on the island first. The motto reads 'Out of Many, One People.'

old: A 1954 five-centavo coin from Argentina, from Juan Perón's second presidency. The side shown has a large 5 with CENTAVOS and the date, and REPUBLICA ARGENTINA around the rim; the other side of this series carries a portrait of José de San Martín, the general who led Argentina to independence.
